body:
Founder real-time: 'continue working on parena editor' (continuation).

Closed a real gap: sdl2/key-left and sdl2/key-right were added alongside key-backspace/key-return earlier the same day but never actually wired into a real edit loop. stdlib/editor/buffer.prn gained move-cursor-left/move-cursor-right (plain Buffer-returning, clamped at both edges rather than Result-wrapped -- an arrow key at the line's start/end is a real no-op, not an error). Wired into examples/editor_main.c's real event loop.

Verified with real tests: moving the cursor left then inserting text lands the new text at the real, moved position (not just checking the cursor's own reported value) -- 'Hello' -> move left twice -> insert 'X' -> genuinely 'HelXlo', confirming the cursor position actually drives where edits land. Real clamping confirmed at both buffer edges. Clean under -Werror and ASan+UBSan. Zero regression in the full suite + make editor-demo-smoke.

Commit: 986dc91.

⚓ ☃
title: Real Left/Right arrow-key cursor movement wired into the PARENA editor
